gates.evidence: The proposal uses the AI character 'Explain quantum physics simply.' for the game partner, which is SFW.
The reward is 30 minutes of 'Upgrade to Luzia+' access, not a click, install, or rating.
The offer appears after a decline, offering a sample rather than punishing the user.
The storyboard includes an opt-in card with 'Play to try' and 'No thanks' buttons.
The offer text explicitly states 'Play a 15-second game to try 30 minutes of Upgrade to Luzia+ now.'
The offer card contains a 'No thanks' button.
Triggered on the Services Tab only after the account sheet is dismissed.
Proposal explicitly limits eligibility to 'Guests who just declined the account sheet'.

scores.evidence: The offer triggers immediately after the user declines the account sheet (m2), precisely when they are at a wall, providing a sample of the missed entitlement.
The proposal is native, offering a sample of the very feature just blocked. It does not degrade free services.
High safety: gated to decliners, capped at once a day, and time-boxed (30 mins). It uses sampling to drive future subscription value.
Cost to serve is zero, while revenue per view is positive ($0.009-$0.015).
Targeting decliners of the account wall is a significant part of the guest user journey, though less than 100% of DAU.
Maps directly to SIM-RWD units with standard SSV and remote config.
Uses Luzia specific terms: 'Upgrade to Luzia+', 'Services Tab', 'Explain quantum physics simply.', 'Create Account Sheet'.
Explicitly capped at once per day, avoiding nagging.
Planned metrics include subscription conversion rates, D7 retention, and a 10% intent-to-treat user-level holdout.

parsed.topConcern: None, the proposal is well-designed and aligns with the knowledge base.
